First market of the morning still smelled like frost. I pulled back the canvas and there she was already, hood pulled low, crouched in front of the cart.

"Morning. Hand mirror's eight coppers today, blanket's twelve. Looking's free."

Mio didn't answer. She just turned her face toward the very back shelf, the way she always does. She never buys anything and she never asks a price. She just tips one ear, a little.

Under the Customer Service Department's policy, a person who doesn't buy isn't a customer, and non-customers get shooed off. The Customer Service Department is me, by the way. So is the person who wrote the policy. So today I didn't shoo.

I tore my bread in half and held it out. Mio thought about it for a second, then took it.

"...Thank you."

It was the first time I'd ever heard her talk. Deeper than I expected, and I was so surprised that I was the one who ran out of words. A merchant at a loss for words is more embarrassing than a bad wholesale price.

We ate side by side while the frost melted and the market filled up.

Half a loaf of bread this morning: one copper. Putting it on her tab.
